intro.p: I'm Nishant Suria [nɪʃɑ̃nt sɹ̩iə], a graduate student in Computational Linguistics at SJSU. The majority of my previous work has been in Phonetics and Phonology, but I'm passionate about the entire breadth of linguistics. My specific interests are in Indic and Dravidian languages, text-to-speech systems, and language contact.

0.title: Acquisition of Sentence-Final Particles across Languages
0.desc: A cross-linguistic investigation of childhood acquisition of Sentence-Final Particles in Mandarin, Japanese, and Vietnamese.

1.title: Vocaloid, VocaloidAI, and Nuances of Singing Voice Synthesis
1.desc: A phonetic and cross-cultural analysis of concatentative and neural singing voice synthesizers, principally Yamaha's VOCALOID.

2.title: On the Coexistence of Arbitrariness and Iconicity, Evidence from Sign Languages
2.desc: An critical look at the linguistic concept of arbitrariness against the frequency of iconic forms in sign langauges.

3.title: A Phonetic Investigation of the Retroflex Approximant in Tamil
3.desc: A phonetic analysis of the Tamil's five distinct liquid consonants, concentrating specifically on /ɻ/, which is gradually merging with /ɭ/ in urban dialects. Pilot study with seven speakers. (Undergraduate Capstone Project)

4.title: Analysis of Vowel Devioicing in Standard Japanese
4.desc: Applying Optimality Theory to phonological devoicing of vowels, principally high vowels, in Standard Japanese.

1.q: Can you tell my friend that [emerging linguistic feature] is an abberation of language?
1.a: No. Today's slang is tomorrow's grammar.

2.a: This is a nonsensical question. While records of written Old Tamil date back to the 3rd century BCE, this was before the divergence of Tamil from its closest relative, Malayalam (9th century CE). Not only is this Tamil inscrutable to modern speakers, it would be just as apt to call it Old Malayalam instead. Ultimately, Old Tamil itself is theorized to derive from the South branch of Proto-Dravidian.

0.blurb: This bird had attitude. The little guy seemed to have a desire to be photographed, hence I was able to get such up-close shot. I thought I'd never seen this bird before, but it seems that this bird simply looks starkly different as a juvenile, with brown patterned plumes instead of the normal solid white and gray. I suppose, I too am quite different from my juvenile self.

1.tagline: Literally the most bird of all time
1.blurb: These birds were very bird-like in nature. They were numerous, and got up to all sorts of bird-like activities such as perching on things.

2.tagline: A blue, jay, not a blue jay.
2.blurb: There is something unsettlingly beautiful to me about blue birds. As always, they elude my attempts to photograph them. This was a lucky clearish picture among tens of attempts. Apparently, Steller's Jay has thirteen recognized subspecies, and by look this seems to be C. s. annectens, however this subspecies isn't known to live around Yosemite.

3.blurb: This pigeon called for a good picture. Unfortunately, I could not deliver, and this one will have to suffice. This is likely one of my favorite pigeons in my collection. This pigeon reminds us to be ourselves, and to find meaning in our own uniqueness. Strolling Manhattan, among many shades of people, it was equally heartwarming to see many shades of rock pigeons.

4.blurb: We were not sufficiently prepared for how cold Aomori was going to be. Shivering, we happened upon the same exact ducks that we see at home, A. platyrhynchos, in a snowed-over local shrine scouring small fish in the frigid water.

5.blurb: In my first trip to Europe, I bore witness to pigeons of shades I had never seen before. But this is my favorite. Looks exactly like the normal pattern of a rock pigeon, just sepia-shifted.

6.blurb: Oldest picture of pigeons in my collection, before I gained fondness of photographing them. Indian pigeons are almost identical to the prototypical rock pigeon, with little variation. They seem to have a slender neck and torso compared to those in the United States, but I assume this has a lot more to do with diet than any physiological difference.
